nameStory: Coelastrum microporum doesn't have a widely-used common name, so scientists stick with its scientific name. The genus name 'Coelastrum' comes from Greek words meaning 'hollow star,' perfectly describing how these tiny algae arrange themselves in beautiful, star-like hollow spheres. The species name 'microporum' means 'small pores,' referring to the tiny openings between the cells in their geometric colonies.
description: Coelastrum microporum is a microscopic freshwater green algae that you'll never see with the naked eye - it's only about 20-50 micrometers across (smaller than the width of a human hair!). [UNCERTAIN: Specific size range] This tiny organism forms stunning geometric colonies that look like hollow, perforated spheres or stars when viewed under a microscope. Each colony is made up of 8-32 individual cells arranged in a single layer, creating intricate patterns with small gaps between them. While invisible to us, these algae play important roles in freshwater ecosystems as food for tiny water creatures.

funFact: Despite being invisible to the naked eye, a single drop of pond water can contain thousands of these geometric masterpieces - each one a perfectly engineered hollow sphere that would make any architect jealous of nature's mathematical precision!
confusionNotes: [UNCERTAIN: Specific distinguishing features] Other Coelastrum species form similar hollow colonies, but C. microporum is distinguished by its smaller pore size between cells and specific colony architecture - identification typically requires expert microscopic examination.
